axes.question: Do professional decheteries exist at scale in France: how many, what do they cost artisans (per visit/subscription), what coverage?
Does the decheterie network meet its environmental purpose: diversion/valorisation rates, sorting rejects (refus de tri) at decheteries?
What happens to reusable objects dropped at decheteries: reuse platforms, the 350t/year destroyed estimate?
Has CNIL ever enforced (mises en demeure/sanctions) badge or LAPI access-control processing at collectivites?

causal.cause: Only ~200 professional decheteries exist vs 4,500+ household sites; public pro access is per-tonne priced
causal.effect: Excluded professionals face a thin, paid alternative network
causal.mechanism: Exclusion (AMP 2025) pushes pros to Ecodrop-style paid depots (DIB 188 EUR/t) or public pro tariffs (Caen bulky 298 EUR/t); the cost gap vs free household access creates the wild-dumping incentive

causal.cause: Mixed/contaminated flows and absent sorting capacity at small sites
causal.effect: A quarter of decheterie intake is landfilled without valorisation
causal.mechanism: Official SDES/Insee/Ademe destination split: 43% recycled, 25% composted, 25% landfilled, 6% energy

causal.cause: AGEC-mandated zones reservantes depend on local ressourcerie partnerships
causal.effect: Reuse captures only a fraction of deposited objects
causal.mechanism: Mandatory reuse zones route objects to ESS shops; scale not nationally measured

claims.claim: The alternative for excluded professionals is thin (~200 pro sites) and priced per tonne
claims.gap: No national census of pro decheterie capacity or average artisan cost

claims.claim: Decheteries meet their environmental purpose only partially: 25% of intake is landfilled without valorisation
claims.gap: No per-site refus-de-tri series; national split only

claims.claim: Reuse zones are mandatory (AGEC) but reuse scale is not nationally measured
claims.gap: The 350t/yr destroyed-objects figure remains an OPEN estimate

claims.claim: CNIL enforcement of access-control data rules is real but has never targeted decheterie badge/LAPI processing
claims.gap: Enforcement search bounded to public CNIL communications

facts.subject: Professional decheterie network scarcity
facts.value: Professional decheteries are scarce in France: roughly 200 sites vs 4,500+ household decheteries (Gurdebeke operator estimate, 2026). Coverage gaps force excluded pros to either pay private operators or travel far.

facts.subject: Ecodrop pro depot pricing
facts.value: Ecodrop (IDF, 45 partner pro decheteries, founded 2017): DIB mixed 188 EUR/t, rubble 34 EUR/t, green waste 65 EUR/t, paper/cardboard free; per-visit paid deposits with unique payment codes; explicitly reserved to professionals — the priced alternative excluded pros are pushed toward.

facts.subject: CNIL LAPI enforcement history
facts.value: CNIL enforcement is real but dated and narrow: 25/08/2020 four communes were formally put on notice (mises en demeure) for illegal LAPI verbalisation; communes remain barred from judicial-police LAPI use. No CNIL sanction found to date targeting decheterie badge/access-control processing specifically.

facts.subject: Decheterie environmental outcomes
facts.value: Official SDES/Insee/Ademe data (notre-environnement.gouv.fr, 05/12/2025): decheteries receive 40% of household+assimilated waste (242 kg/hab 2021); of what is deposited: 43% recycled, 25% composted/methanised, 25% landfilled WITHOUT valorisation, 6% energy. A quarter of decheterie intake is buried.

facts.subject: Decheterie reuse zones
facts.value: Nouvelle Fabrique (29/01/2026): AGEC law made 'zones reservantes' (reuse areas) mandatory in public decheteries; partnership networks route reusable objects to ressourceries/ESS shops; 'thousands of objects per year' diverted from bins at their sites — reuse exists but scale is not nationally measured.

facts.subject: Caen la mer professional decheterie tariffs
facts.value: Caen la mer public decheterie pro tariffs (27/07/2026): bulky 298.20 EUR/t, green waste 71.8 EUR/t, wood 134.21 EUR/t — a public network charging pros per-tonne rates far above the household-free baseline.

scope.lead_question: Do professional decheteries exist at scale (cost, coverage) as the alternative for excluded pros; does the decheterie network meet its environmental purpose (valorisation, refus de tri); what happens to reusable objects; has CNIL ever enforced badge/LAPI rules?

sections.ACTOR_NETWORK_MAP: Operators: Veolia (Recycl'Inn Pro), Ecodrop (IDF aggregator, 45 partner sites), Gurdebeke (Compiègne/Clermont), municipal networks (Caen la mer). Regulator: CNIL (LAPI enforcement 2020). ESS: Nouvelle Fabrique + ressourcerie networks. State: SDES/Insee/Ademe (official statistics).
sections.COGNITIVE_MAP: Corpus: 2 operator pages (B family, interest noted), 1 Veolia product page (B), 1 municipal tariff page (A), 1 official SDES/Insee/Ademe explainer (A), 1 ESS operator page (C), 1 CNIL enforcement page (A). Pro-network counts come from an interested operator (Gurdebeke) — treated as estimate.
sections.CONTRADICTION_LEDGER: No direct contradictions. Gurdebeke ~200 pro sites is an interested-party estimate (flagged); official data has no competing count.
sections.CREDO: The exclusion story is incomplete without the alternative: if the pro network is thin and priced, exclusion converts directly into cost pressure on artisans and into wild-dumping incentive. The environmental ledger (what decheteries actually recycle vs bury) tests whether the 1980 promise held.
sections.DIALECTICAL_MAP: Institutional steelman: paid pro access funds real treatment costs; 43%+25% valorisation is comparable to European peers. Adversarial steelman: the 200-vs-4500 count is an operator marketing figure; the 25% landfill share shows the network fails its core promise; CNIL silence on decheterie badges may reflect absence of complaints, not compliance.
sections.EDI_REPORT: Diversity: official statistics (A), operators (B), ESS practitioner (C), regulator enforcement (A). The pro-network count lacks an independent official source — kept at tier ✧ and flagged as estimate.
sections.IMPACT_MAP: Article impact: (1) exclusion axis A gains its missing half — the alternative is thin (~200 pro sites, operator estimate) and priced (34-298 EUR/t), quantifying the pressure pushing pros toward wild dumping; (2) the environmental ledger adds the missing counter-narrative — 25% of decheterie intake is landfilled, so the network fails its 1980 promise partially; (3) reuse zones exist by law but scale is unmeasured; (4) CNIL enforcement is real (2020 LAPI mises en demeure) but has never touched decheterie badges — the retention frappe stands on doctrine, not enforcement precedent.
sections.MANIPULATION_REPORT: INPUT_KIND: TOPIC | MISSION_MODE: INVESTIGATION | SYMBOL_STAGE: CORPUS_FINAL | Operator marketing present (Ecodrop 'finies les galeres', Gurdebeke scarcity claim sells their service) — both flagged as family B with interests noted. Official statistics dominate the environmental ledger.
sections.NEXT_QUERIES: Watch: official pro-decheterie census (ADEME/SINOE), per-site refus-de-tri data in RPQS, CNIL sanction database updates.
sections.RESOURCE_FLOW_MAP: Excluded pros face: private pro depots (Ecodrop DIB 188 EUR/t, rubble 34 EUR/t) or public pro tariffs (Caen: bulky 298.20 EUR/t, wood 134.21 EUR/t, green 71.8 EUR/t) — versus free household access funded by TEOM. Environmental ledger: of 242 kg/hab decheterie intake, 43% recycled, 25% composted, 25% landfilled, 6% energy. Reuse: AGEC-mandated zones reservantes feed ressourceries; scale unmeasured.
sections.RESPONSIBILITY_MAP: Operators (Veolia/Ecodrop/Gurdebeke): price the pro alternative; collectivites: set pro tariffs + reuse zones; CNIL: enforcement posture; ADEME/SDES: the official environmental ledger; ESS networks: reuse execution.
sections.SCOPING_REPORT: OBJECT_QUESTION: what exists as the professional alternative to excluded decheterie access, does the network meet its environmental purpose, what happens to reusable objects, and has CNIL enforced access-control data rules? LEAD_QUESTION: which of these four hares materially change the article's claims?
sections.TEMPORAL_STATE: Source dates: Gurdebeke/Ecodrop/Veolia operator pages accessed 31/08/2026; Caen la mer tariffs 27/07/2026; notre-environnement.gouv.fr 05/12/2025 (2021 data); Nouvelle Fabrique 29/01/2026; CNIL LAPI verbalisation warning 25/08/2020. Investigation date: 31/08/2026.
sections.VERIFICATION_REPORT: All 6 facts verified against inspected sources; each carries >=1 FETCH-inspected source. Refutation searches found no contradicting evidence; operator-sourced counts capped at ✧.
